80154.subject: Blast Is Shutting Down Its Layer 2
80154.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Blast](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/blast-to-shut-down-layer-2-citing-unsustainable-costs)**[ is shutting down its Layer 2 and giving users until Oct. 26 to withdraw](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/blast-to-shut-down-layer-2-citing-unsustainable-costs)

* **[Chainalysis](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-links-387-million-bitget-hack-to-north-korea)**[ tied the $387 million Bitget hack to North Korea](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-links-387-million-bitget-hack-to-north-korea)

* **[Aave Labs](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-labs-proposes-foundation-to-bring-brand-and-ip-under-dao-oversight)**[ proposed a foundation to put Aave's brand and IP under DAO oversight](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-labs-proposes-foundation-to-bring-brand-and-ip-under-dao-oversight)

* **[NEAR Intents](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/near-intents-gm-says-3-8-million-in-hack-funds-returned-in-full)**[ says its attacker returned the $3.8 million in full](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/near-intents-gm-says-3-8-million-in-hack-funds-returned-in-full)

* **[The IMF](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/imf-approves-138-million-for-el-salvador-after-bitcoin-waiver)**[ approved $138 million for El Salvador after waiving missed conditions, Bitcoin included](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/imf-approves-138-million-for-el-salvador-after-bitcoin-waiver)

In June 2024 Blast held $2.2 billion in DeFi deposits and paid users native yield for keeping ETH on its chain. On Friday it said it sees no credible path to making that chain pay for itself, and it is shutting it down.

**Blast** [told users to move their assets to Ethereum by Oct. 26](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/blast-to-shut-down-layer-2-citing-unsustainable-costs), the last day its normal interface will process withdrawals; after that, funds stay recoverable through the bridge contracts directly. About **$63.5 million** still sits in the canonical bridge, and L2BEAT values the stETH component of its secured assets at about $46.8 million. Withdrawals pause first for roughly a week while Blast unwinds its Lido position, then resume with a 24-hour delay.

The feature that pulled deposits in is now what slows them down: native yield meant parking users' ETH in Lido, so every exit waits on that unwind first. Blast joins **Balancer**, whose holders approved a wind-down this week, and **ZetaChain**, which voted in September to retire its chain.

**Read more below!**

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### BLOCKCHAINS

## Blast to Shut Down Layer 2, Citing Unsustainable Costs

**Blast** said on Oct. 2 that [it will shut down its Ethereum Layer 2](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/blast-to-shut-down-layer-2-citing-unsustainable-costs), citing operating costs that exceed revenue: "we do not see a credible path to making the chain economically sustainable." Use

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft US jobs data and fading Fed-hike bets lifted Bitcoin toward $87K, while regulators in Washington and Brussels advanced crypto rulebooks and institutions from Tokyo to Tether pushed deeper into on-chain finance. 📊 Weak US Jobs Report Lifts Bitcoin Toward $87K The US added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the roughly 90,000 economists expected, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000. Bitcoin held its gains and traded just under $87,000 as markets slashed the odds of an October Fed hike to about 13%. Derivatives traders had already piled in: open interest climbed by roughly $2.3 billion since Sept. 30, and perpetual funding rates rose from about 3% to 10%. Read full story → 🏛️ SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules as Peirce Exits The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed a dedicated custody framework for registered investment advisers and regulated funds holding crypto. Advisers could act as custodians themselves in limited cases, such as when no permitted custodian exists for an asset, and state-chartered trust companies would qualify as custodians. Chair Paul Atkins said the plan creates a compliant pathway where none existed. A 60-day comment period opens after Federal Register publication. The proposal lands as Commissioner Hester Peirce, architect of the Crypto Task Force, departs on Friday, leaving the SEC with only two commissioners. More details → 🇸🇻 IMF Waives El Salvador's Bitcoin Breach, Releases $139M The IMF board completed the second and third reviews of El Salvador's $1.4 billion loan program and released roughly $139 million, granting a waiver even though the country breached its limit on Bitcoin accumulation. The Fund accepted documentation that the extra coins came from private donations rather than public money, but said no further accumulation is envisaged beyond documented gifts. The program also requires a smaller state role in the Chivo wallet, now majority-controlled by a private operator. Read more → 💵 Tether's USDT Is Coming Home to Bitcoin Tether's USDT, which first launched on Bitcoin's Omni Layer in 2014 before migrating to Ethereum and Tron, is set to return to Bitcoin this month. Tether-backed Utexo, which holds a commercial license to issue the token on Bitcoin, will use the RGB protocol to enable private USDT transfers, direct BTC-USDT swaps
